title: Multi-regulator of EZH2-PPARs Therapeutic Targets: A Hallmark for Prospective Restoration of Pancreatic Insulin Production and Cancer Dysregulation.
authors: Olowosoke, Christopher Busayo; Gbemisola, Otitoola; Alaba, Adebola Abosede; Adepoju, Oluwadamilola Hope; Okorie, Benson; Odjegba, Peace Ifeoma; Ogunsanmi, Ayomide Oluwaseyi; Oke, Grace Ayomide; Akinlolu, Oluwatoyin; Olubena, Tomiwa Lois; Bello, Ridwan Opeyemi; Adegboyega, Benjamin Babatunde
one_liner_zh: 该文通过虚拟筛选、对接和DFT研究EZH2-PPARs靶点与天然产物的结合，但核心是蛋白-小分子药物靶点，而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，仅涉及蛋白网络和对接，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: The unexpected rise in cancer and diabetes statistics has been a significant global threat, inciting ongoing research into various biomarkers that can act as innovative therapeutic targets for their management. The recent discovery of how EZH2-PPARs' regulatory function affects the metabolic and signalling pathways contributing to this disease has posed a significant breakthrough, with the synergistic combination of inhibitors like GSK-126 and bezafibrate for treating these diseases. Nonetheless, no findings on other protein biomarkers involved in the associated side effects have been reported. As a result of this virtual study, we identified the gene-disease association, protein interaction networks between EZH2-PPARs and other protein biomarkers regulating pancreatic cancer and diabetes pathology, ADME/Toxicity profiling, docking simulation and density functional theory of some natural products. The results indicated a correlation between obesity and hypertensive disease for the investigated biomarkers. At the same time, the predicted protein network validates the link to cancer and diabetes, and nine natural products were screened to have versatile binding capacity against the targets. Among all natural products, phytocassane A outperforms the standard drugs' (GSK-126 and bezafibrate) in silico validation for drug-likeness profiles. Hence, these natural products were conclusively proposed for additional experimental screening to complement the results on their utility in drug development for diabetes and cancer therapy against the EZH2-PPARs' new target.
abstract_zh: 癌症和糖尿病统计数据的意外上升已成为一项重大的全球性威胁，促使人们持续研究各种生物标志物，这些标志物可作为其管理中的创新治疗靶点。近期发现EZH2-PPARs的调控功能如何影响导致该疾病的代谢和信号通路，这构成了一项重大突破，其中抑制剂如GSK-126和苯扎贝特（bezafibrate）的协同组合用于治疗这些疾病。尽管如此，尚未有关于参与相关副作用的其他蛋白生物标志物的研究发现被报道。通过这项虚拟研究，我们确定了基因-疾病关联、EZH2-PPARs与其他调控胰腺癌和糖尿病病理的蛋白生物标志物之间的蛋白质相互作用网络、ADME/毒性分析、一些天然产物的对接模拟和密度泛函理论。结果表明，所研究的生物标志物与肥胖和高血压疾病之间存在相关性。同时，预测的蛋白质网络验证了与癌症和糖尿病的关联，并筛选出九种天然产物对靶点具有多功能的结合能力。在所有天然产物中，稻壳素A（phytocassane A）在药物相似性特征的计算机模拟验证中优于标准药物（GSK-126和苯扎贝特）。因此，这些天然产物被最终提议用于额外的实验筛选，以补充其在针对EZH2-PPARs新靶点的糖尿病和癌症治疗药物开发中的效用结果。
